prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1261; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle was reversing out of a space when it contacted the claimant's parked vehicle. Insured states the other vehicle was not visible at the time. Photos of both vehicles requested and received. Liability appears probable against insured pending review of lot camera footage.

Entry 2: Claimant has reported a wrist fracture sustained when she stepped out of her vehicle and fell during the impact. Medical records requested. Claimant is represented by counsel; all further contact to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and placed in file.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. They confirmed the fracture was treated with a closed reduction and a cast, and that follow-up orthopedic appointments are scheduled. Requested itemized medical bills, wage loss documentation, and any prior records of wrist complaints. Attorney indicated a demand package will follow once treatment is complete.

Entry 4: Reviewed the lot security footage obtained from the property manager. Footage shows the insured vehicle backing into the claimant's vehicle at low speed while the claimant was seated in the driver's seat. Insured appears to have failed to check blind spots before reversing. Liability assessment updated to reflect insured as primarily at fault. Notified the insured's property damage and bodily injury coverage handlers.

Entry 5: Independent appraiser assigned to the claimant's vehicle. Estimate received for rear quarter panel repair and bumper replacement. Reserve adjusted to reflect the estimate and the anticipated bodily injury exposure. Supervisor review requested due to attorney involvement and the nature of the injury. Next step is to await medical documentation before evaluating settlement range.
